FERDINAND TUBBAN Provincial Governor Province of Kalinga Capitol Hills, Bulanao, Tabuk City Dear Governor Tubban: S. 202 This is in reference to the letter dated 31 March 2019 of former Governor Jocel Baac requesting for clarification on the following issues, which we quote in toto: l. "Whether or not there was a quorum when the Sanggunian of the MLGU of Rizal, Kalinga passed SB Resolution No. 2019-11 and SB Resolution No. 2019-20 which seeks to affirm SB Resolution No. 2019-11. 2. What kind of majority vote is required in passing a Resolution that will authorize the Acting Municipal Mayor of Rizal, Kalinga to enter into a MOA with the DA-RFO-CAR?" On the first query, the herein provision of Republic Act No 7160 otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC) is applicable, viz: Section 53. Quorum. — (a) A matQrity of all the members of the sanggunian who have been elected and qualified shall constitute a quorum to transact official business. Should a question of quorum be raised during a session, the presiding officer shall immediately proceed to call the roll of the members and thereafter announce the results. Based on the above-cited provision, the law requires that the majority of all members of sanggunian who have been duly elected and qualified should constitute the same. In the case of Rizal, Kalinga, it was represented that the Sanggunian Bayan (SB) was originally composed of ten (IO) members including the Vice Mayor. However, three (3) SB members were dismissed from Office while the Mayor was page 1 Of 4

suspended by the Office of the Ombudsman. Thus, the Vice Mayor assumed temporarily the Office of the Mayor while the "most senior" SB sits as the Acting Vice Mayor. It was further represented that after the Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) Elections, the SK Pederasyon President sits as an ex officio member of the SB, thereby resulting to seven (7) total members in the Sanggunian including the Acting Vice Mayor. Now, the Province of Kalinga is inquiring if the there is a quorum during a session with the presence of only four (4) SB Members, including the Presiding Officer. In reply to this, the case of Javier vs Cadiaol is instructive. It provides: "Verily, the Vice Governor, as the SP's Presiding Officerz should be counted for purposes of ascertaining the existence ofa quorum,xxx. " Thus, the Presiding officer is counted in order to determine if the quorum exists. As to the computation of quorum, may we refer you to the case of Santiago vs. Guingona, et al.2 which states that: "The term "majority" has been judicially defined a number of times. When referring to a certain number out ofa total or aggregate, "means the number greater than half qr more than half Qf any total. " To further elucidate, there are two (2) ways to determine the majority: 1. that which is fifty percent plus one (500/0+1) of the entire membership, or 2. that which is simply more than one half (1/2) of the entire membership. In the case of Rizal, Kalinga, since there were seven (7) total members remaining in the SB that were duly elected and qualified, the quorum should be computed in this manner: 7/2=3.5 (3.5 is the 50%) 3.5 + 1 = 4.5 or can be reduced to 4 It was shown above that 4 is more than half (i.e. 3.5). Hence, the total number required to constitute a quorum is only 4 and not 4.5 or 5. Therefore, in view of the foregoing, this Department opines that the said SB session was with a quorum. G.R. NO. 185369, August 03, 2016 2 G.R. No. 134577, 18 November 1998 Page 2 of 4

1. In the second query, this Department opines that the majority vote required by law is only simple majority. The LGC and its Implementing Rules and Regulation (IRR) provide: Section 22. Corporate Powers. — (b) xxx (c) (c) Unless otherwise provided in this Code, no contract may be entered into Che local chief executive in behalf of the local government unit without prior authorization by the sanggunian concerned. A legible copy of such contract shall be posted at a conspicuous place in the provincial capitol or the city, municipal or barangay hall. Article 107 of the IRR: ARTICLE 107. Ordinances and Resolutions. — The following rules shall govern the enactment of ordinances and resolutions: xxx (g) No ordinance or resolution passed by the sanggunian in a regular or special session duly called for the purpose shall be valid unless approved by a maiority of the members present. there being a quorum. Any ordinance or resolution authorizing or directing the payment of money or creating liability, Shal/ require the affirmative vote of a majority Qf all the sanggunian members for its passage. Based on the above-cited provisions of the LGC and the IRR, the general rule is that ordinance or resolution should only be approved by a majority of the members of the sanggunian present, there being a quorum. The exception provided by the IRR is when it directs a payment of money or creates liability, the required vote is qualified majority, that is, majority of all the SB members. In the letter, former Gov. Baac represented that the questioned project is a downloading by the Department of Agriculture (DA) of the amount of Two Hundred Forty Million Pesos (Php 240,000,000.00) to the LGU of Rizal, Kalinga for the rehabilitation of various Farm-to-Market Roads (FMRs) in the said municipality. In line with this, it appears that the MOA pertains to the project granted by the National Government, thru the DA, to the LGU of Rizal, Kalinga. Hence, it does not create indebtedness by the LGU to the DA. Accordingly, second paragraph of Article 107 of the IRR of LGC, which requires qualified majority for ordinance or resolution authorizing or directing the payment of money or creating liability is not applicable herein. page 3 of 4

Henceforth, we reiterate that the vote required is only majority of the members present, provided there is a quorum. It must be further noted that in counting the votes for passing the said Resolution, the case of Javier vs. Cadia03 further said: "Verily. the Vice Governor, as the SP's Presiding Officer, should be counted for purposes of ascertaining the existence of a quorum, Out not in the determination of the required number of votes necessary to uphold a matter Vefpre the In sum, the Presiding Officer is counted in the determination of the quorum but during the counting of votes for the passage of a resolution or an ordinance, his/her vote should not be counted, unless there is a tie. Applying this principle in the case at hand, since there is a quorum with the presence of 4 members (I presiding officer and 3 SB members) thus, the required number of votes to pass the resolution is only 2 {1.5 (50% of 3)+1 = 2.5 or only 2 because it is more than 50%)}. Therefore, if 3 voted in the affirmative, then the resolution had been validly passed by the Sanggunian of Rizal, Kalinga. We hope we had addressed the concerns accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: MARIVEL C. ACENDONCILLO, CESO 111 Undersecretary Copy furnished: DIR.
